entities.summary: Michu of Silla was the thirteenth ruler of the Korean state of Silla, marking the beginning of the Kim clan's dominance of the throne. Born to Gudo, a prominent Silla general, and Kim Alji, the sixth-generation descendant of the clan's founder, Michu ascended to power in 269 CE. His reign was characterized by a series of military campaigns against neighboring states, including the Goguryeo and Baekje kingdoms, which further solidified Silla's position as a major power in the peninsula. Despite his military successes, Michu's rule was also marked by internal power struggles and economic stagnation, which would eventually lead to his downfall. His legacy as a key figure in Silla's later history remains significant, with the Kim clan continuing to hold the throne for over two centuries. Michu's reign is also notable for its cultural achievements, including the development of Silla's unique writing system and the promotion of Buddhism throughout the kingdom. Ultimately, Michu's reign came to an end in 284 CE, when he was succeeded by his son, Gyeongmyeong. Despite his relatively short time on the throne, Michu's impact on Silla's history was profound, and his name remains an important figure in the study of Korean history.
